items.name: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
items.what_it_models: Provenance of resources: activities, entities, and agents involved in producing, influencing, or delivering a piece of data or thing; supports expressing lineage, derivation chains, and attribution for any resource including legal documents and derived records.

evidence.quote: The PROV Ontology (PROV-O) expresses the PROV Data Model using the OWL2 Web Ontology Language (OWL2).
W3C Recommendation 30 April 2013
An prov:Entity is a physical, digital, conceptual, or other kind of thing with some fixed aspects
An prov:Agent is something that bears some form of responsibility for an activity taking place

items.name: Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) / ISO 17442
items.governing_body: GLEIF (Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation) / ISO TC68
items.licence: public good, available free of charge to all users

items.name: Verifiable LEI (vLEI) / ISO 17442-3
items.what_it_models: Verifiable digital credentials that cryptographically bind a legal entity's LEI-confirmed identity to the personal identity and organizational role of an individual acting on behalf of that entity; enables automated chain-of-trust verification of who signed an agreement on behalf of which company.
core_concepts: Legal Entity Official Organizational Role vLEI Credential
Legal Entity Engagement Context Role vLEI Credential

evidence.quote: The vLEI cryptographically combines three identity sources: the entity's identity, confirmed by their LEI, an individual's personal identity, and the official organizational role they hold.
In 2024, a third update to the LEI standard, ISO 17442-3, defined and standardized the use of vLEIs as digital credentials across the global LEI ecosystem.
The vLEI issuance system establishes GLEIF as the digital 'root of trust'.

items.name: European Legislation Identifier (ELI)
items.governing_body: Publications Office of the European Union
items.what_it_models: Identification, metadata description, and point-in-time versioning of European and national legislation; assigns URIs to legislative acts and provides an OWL ontology following FRBR principles to express relationships between versions, expressions, and formats of laws, plus cross-border legislative references.

evidence.quote: The European Legislation Identifier (ELI) is a standard that makes it easier to identify and describe legislation across Europe.

items.name: URN:LEX — URN Namespace for Sources of Law (RFC 9676)
items.what_it_models: Persistent, location-independent, language-neutral unique identifiers for sources of law (legislation, case law, administrative acts, regulations) across any jurisdiction; applies the FRBR Work/Expression/Manifestation/Item hierarchy to legal documents to support point-in-time versioning and language variants.

evidence.quote: LEX, a Uniform Resource Name (URN) namespace identifier that identifies, names, assigns, and manages persistent resources in the legal domain.
The purpose of the LEX namespace is to assign a unique identifier in a well-defined format to documents that are sources of law.
Identifies the scope (state, regional, municipal, supranational, or organizational) where a set of sources of law have validity.

items.name: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
items.licence: W3C Software and Document Notice and License
items.what_it_models: Tamper-evident, cryptographically verifiable credentials representing claims about a subject; provides the data model for digitally signed assertions about identity, authorizations, qualifications, and provenance that can be issued, held, and verified by distinct parties — applicable to signing authority, party credentials, and document authenticity.

evidence.quote: a tamper-evident credential whose authorship can be cryptographically verified
The value of the @context property MUST be an ordered set where the first item is a URL with the value https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2

items.name: Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.1
items.what_it_models: Globally unique, persistent, cryptographically verifiable identifiers for subjects (persons, organizations, documents) that do not require a central registration authority; each DID resolves to a DID Document containing cryptographic keys and service endpoints enabling verifiable interactions.

evidence.quote: Decentralized identifiers (DIDs) are a new type of identifier that enables verifiable, decentralized digital identity.
DIDs are URIs that associate a DID subject with a DID document allowing trustable interactions associated with that subject.
A globally unique persistent identifier that does not require a centralized registration authority and is often generated and/or registered cryptographically.

items.name: Digital Object Identifier System (DOI) / ISO 26324
items.what_it_models: Persistent, semantically interoperable identifiers for intellectual content objects (documents, data sets, standards) that resolve to current metadata and location regardless of where the object moves; relevant for giving legal instruments and their versions persistent, citable, resolvable identities.

evidence.quote: The DOI system utilises the Handle System as one component in building an added value application, for the persistent, semantically interoperable, identification of intellectual property entities.
Persistence is a function of organizations, not of technology; a persistent identifier system requires a persistent organization and defined processes.

items.name: DCMI Metadata Terms (provenance vocabulary)

evidence.quote: A statement of any changes in ownership and custody of the resource since its creation that are significant for its authenticity, integrity, and interpretation.
The statement may include a description of any changes successive custodians made to the resource.

evidence.quote: DALICC stands for Data License Clearance Center. It is a software framework that supports application developers, legal experts and sales managers in the legally secure reutilization of third party digital sources such as data, content or software.

items.name: ISDA Common Domain Model (CDM)
items.governing_body: ISDA, ISLA, ICMA; hosted by FINOS (Fintech Open Source Foundation)
items.what_it_models: Financial products, bilateral trades and post-trade lifecycle events as structured, machine-executable Rosetta DSL objects; models Party, Product, Trade, TradeState, Execution, LegalAgreement, and composable BusinessEvents (clearing, settlement, option exercise). evidence.quote: The Common Domain Model (CDM) is a standardized, machine-readable and machine-executable model that represents financial products, trades in those products and the lifecycle events of those trades.
The CDM is developed through the community specification open governance process, and underlying code assets are released under the Community Specification License 1.0.
A trade state is defined in CDM by the `TradeState` data type and represents the state of a trade at each stage in its lifecycle.
A business event represents a life cycle event of a trade. The combination of the state changes results in a qualifiable life cycle event.
all legal agreements must contain an agreement date, two contractual parties, and information indicating the published form of market standard agreement being used.
A financial product describes a thing that is used to transfer financial risk between two parties.
